claims.text: Lattice distortion governs the overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding.
Dislocation glide governs the overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding.
Grain-boundary sliding governs the overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding.
Changing alloy composition can optimize the high-temperature mechanical response of a high-entropy-alloy coating.
Changing processing conditions can optimize lattice distortion, dislocation glide, and grain-boundary sliding in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The proposed composition and processing changes will improve wear resistance relative to the stated baseline.
The proposed composition and processing changes will reduce microscopic deformation relative to the stated baseline.
The predicted effects are intended to hold in a high-temperature operating regime.
Coating thickness may affect the observed wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
Surface roughness may affect the observed wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
Environmental conditions may affect the observed wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
The baseline is an uncoated conventional metal substrate.

contradictions.description: The intervention and experiment vary coating composition and processing, but the stated baseline is an uncoated substrate. This does not isolate the effects of composition or processing from the effect of adding a coating.
